correctness.rationale: The two bipartition classes have ten vertices each and degree three. Connectedness follows, for example, because two 2-subsets differing by one element share a neighbouring 3-subset, and the graph of such replacements is connected. The graph genus is 11. Bipartition-preserving automorphisms preserve the common-neighbour graph on 2-subsets, whose five maximal 4-cliques are the five label-stars of K5; they act faithfully by permuting these, as the opposite vertices have distinct neighbour sets. Complement swaps classes and commutes with S5. On the split curve three distinct marked points on each component make every graph symmetry extend uniquely over k and preclude a kernel; constant-group descent over a procyclic Galois group gives 7 times 2 classes. The local-to-global tangent map for nodal deformations surjects onto the node-smoothing lines and there is no obstruction (the local obstruction sheaf vanishes and the local Ext^1 sheaf is supported at nodes). For a twisted fibre each orbit of node-lines descends to a line over its residue field, so admits a nonzero first-order parameter. Formal smoothness lifts this direction over k[[t]], and the ample dualizing line bundle allows projective algebraization. Each local parameter is a unit times t, giving regularity and smoothing all nodes; flat proper connectedness of the geometric special fibre and smoothness away from nodes give a geometrically smooth and connected generic fibre. Raynaud's equivariant identification with the degree-zero Laplacian quotient applies to every such regular thickness-one model. The reduced matrix R presents the quotient in the sink difference basis; the coinvariants add the columns of P-I. The perfect invariant pairing identifies fixed points with the dual of coinvariants, so their invariant factors agree even when an automorphism has order divisible by a group prime. A fresh exact Smith computation independently gives (4,8,40,40,120) and all fourteen tabulated fixed groups including order 2 at the complemented (3,2). The determinant 6,144,000 also follows from viewing the graph as the bipartite double cover of Petersen: its Laplacian uses paired eigenvalues 3±3, 3±1 (five times), 3±(-2) (four times), and the product of nonzeros divided by 20 gives the determinant. The frozen script was inspected, not run. Replay of the independent exact computation: /workspace/branches/8c870185-f1ba-4d04-96a5-8b582b04071d/independent_desargues.py and independent_desargues.out. The computation checks the invariant factors, not the deformation or monodromy theorems.
